question: Should ClawHub sign the existing stored hosted-feed publication contract, and which public URL, key id, trust root, schema version, and rollout path should OpenClaw clients trust?
rationale: Feed signing changes a client trust boundary and production secret contract, while current repository intent keeps signed envelopes behind a separate key-management decision.

options.title: Sign Stored Publications
options.body: Require the signer to wrap the current stored feed payload, preserve exact integrity semantics, and document key rollout before merge.

options.title: Approve A New Signed Contract
options.body: Approve a distinct signed feed schema only after matching OpenClaw parser, route, and compatibility behavior are documented.

options.title: Pause Signing
options.body: Leave this draft parked until the ClawHub signing design, production secrets, and OpenClaw trust root are ready to land together.

recommendation.title: Sign Stored Publications
recommendation.body: Require the signer to wrap the current stored feed payload, preserve exact integrity semantics, and document key rollout before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current hosted OpenClaw plugin feed contract and are the clearest routing owner for changes to its trust boundary.
